ideas.title: Why the Octopus Has Three Hearts #Shorts
ideas.concept: Explain that an octopus has three hearts, and two of them stop pumping while it swims.
ideas.hook: An octopus has three hearts—and swimming makes two of them stop.
ideas.keyVisual: Real close-up octopus footage crawling over a reef, followed by a clear underwater swimming shot and a simple on-screen three-heart diagram.

ideas.title: Why the Gecko Walks on Glass Without Glue #Shorts
ideas.concept: Reveal how microscopic toe hairs create enough molecular attraction for a gecko to climb smooth surfaces.
ideas.hook: This lizard can run up glass without glue, suction, or sticky feet.
ideas.keyVisual: Real gecko close-up climbing a window or smooth wall, with a macro insert of its toes and a clean graphic showing the toe-pad hairs.

ideas.title: Why the Sperm Whale Holds Its Breath for 90 Minutes #Shorts
ideas.concept: Show how sperm whales prepare for extreme dives by storing oxygen in blood and muscle.
ideas.hook: A sperm whale can disappear underwater for up to 90 minutes without taking a breath.
ideas.keyVisual: Real sperm whale surface-and-dive footage with a dramatic tail fluke, underwater descent, and a restrained oxygen-storage diagram.
